data.why: The repository ships ready-to-use example spectra (single-spectrum template and a 12-spectrum botanical batch CSV with empty ri column, which the app accepts) that exactly match the app's required mz,intensity and spectrum_id,mz,intensity,ri CSV schemas.

goals: Upload or paste a single EI mass spectrum and get a ranked list of the ten closest library candidate identities with spectral similarity scores
Judge whether the top-ranked candidate can be trusted using the machine-learning reliability (library-label agreement) score and the top1-top2 margin
Apply the standard or strict confidence-screening rule to decide whether a tentative annotation should be flagged for further review
Upload a batch CSV of multiple spectra (grouped by spectrum_id) and get a one-row-per-spectrum summary of the leading annotation for each
Download the ranked candidate table and/or the batch results as CSV to document or share the annotation session
Understand the method's provenance and limitations (reference library size, SHA-256-verified source, retrospective evaluation accuracy) before relying on a result

review.summary: The tree states the tool's purpose well (tentative library annotation of EI spectra, a trust judgment from similarity, the top-two margin and the model score, Standard/Strict screening, CSV export with provenance), has sensible single and batch phases, and its screens largely support what it says. It needs small corrections before filing: the provenance-export feature overstates what the candidate CSV contains and links to the wrong task, the method/provenance disclosure panel deserves its own feature, and the batch 're-screen' claim rests on the CSV rather than on a cited screen.
